extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing manuscripts for the Annals of Applied Probability and other IMS journals
extracted.subtask_short: preparing Annals of Applied Probability manuscripts
extracted.subtask_description: Collect and follow resources and technical/style requirements referenced by the Annals of Applied Probability (IMS) for preparing and submitting manuscripts, including bibliographic tools, classification schemes, TeX/PDF tool recommendations, and English style references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use MathSciNet to identify references
rubrics_metrics.description: MathSciNet is the on-line version of Mathematical Reviews and is very useful in identifying references related to a paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing is by author, title, keywords, classification numbers, and all words in reviews. Use MathSciNet to locate and verify bibliographic references relevant to your manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Current Index to Statistics for bibliographic searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Current Index to Statistics is a bibliographic index to publications in statistics and related fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indexing is by title and keywords. Use it as an additional resource to find related literature in statistics and adjacent areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use MR Lookup to find exact references
rubrics_metrics.description: MR Lookup is a convenient tool for finding the exact reference for a particular paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use MR Lookup when you need precise bibliographic entries (MR numbers, exact titles/authors) for citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use MSC 2010 classification
rubrics_metrics.description: MSC 2010 is the standard subject classification scheme used in the Annals and other major journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assign appropriate MSC 2010 codes to your manuscript to indicate subject classification as required by the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use standard journal title abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard Journal Title Abbreviations are provided by Mathematical Reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When abbreviating journal titles in references, use the standard abbreviations from Mathematical Reviews to ensure consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide files in standard TeX/PDF formats (use MiKTeX on Windows)
rubrics_metrics.description: MiKTeX is a free TeX program for Windows. It includes standard TeX and LaTeX, a dvi viewer, conversion software to produce postscript and pdf files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare manuscripts using standard TeX/LaTeX tools; on Windows, authors may use MiKTeX to generate DVI/PS/PDF outputs suitable for submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check PostScript output with Ghostview
rubrics_metrics.description: Ghostview is a free postscript viewer available for most computer systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Ghostview (or equivalent PS/PDF viewers) to inspect generated PostScript files to ensure figures and formatting render correctly before submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check PDF output with Adobe Acrobat Reader
rubrics_metrics.description: The Adobe Acrobat Reader is a free PDF viewer available for most computer systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a standard PDF reader (e.g., Acrobat Reader) to verify the final PDF exactly matches intended formatting and content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow authoritative English style and grammar guides
rubrics_metrics.description: Classic references for English usage can be found at Bartleby.com and include The Elements of Style, The King’s English, and the American Heritage Book of English Usage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For grammar and style questions use standard references (e.g., Strunk & White, Fowler, American Heritage). The Guide to Grammar and Style by Jack Lynch is also recommended for students and other writers. The alt.usage.english FAQ may provide alternate positions if you disagree with other guides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to journal-specific manuscript preparation and supplement instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: The site lists 'Manuscript Preparation' and 'Supplement Instructions' (and related pages) for Annals of Applied Probability and multiple IMS journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult and follow the specific 'Manuscript Preparation' and 'Supplement Instructions' pages for the journal you are submitting to (Annals of Applied Probability, Annals of Statistics, Annals of Applied Statistics, etc.) for formatting, submission file requirements, and supplement handling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe editorial policies and procedures for handling manuscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: Links to 'Editorial Policy' and 'Procedures for Handling Manuscripts' are provided for IMS journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of the journal's editorial policies (scope, editorial decisions) and manuscript handling procedures (submission, review, revision) as they affect preparation and submission practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to ethical principles for authors, referees, and editors
rubrics_metrics.description: The site references 'Ethical Principles' for authors, referees, associate editors and editors for several journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with the stated ethical principles (e.g., authorship, disclosure, originality, conflicts of interest) required by IMS journals when preparing and submitting manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult journal-specific resources for authors and referees
rubrics_metrics.description: For each IMS journal (e.g., Annals of Applied Probability, Annals of Statistics, Statistical Science, etc.) the site links resources: Editorial Policy, Contacts, Published Papers, Manuscript Preparation, Supplement Instructions, Guidelines for Referees, and other pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the journal-specific 'Resources for Authors' pages to find detailed submission instructions, contact info, editorial board, and referee guidelines relevant to your submission.
